paper.title_en: How elastic unitarity governs resonance peaks and residue phases
paper.abstract_en: Imposing elastic unitarity on resonant amplitudes yields a geometric rule connecting the reaction threshold, S-matrix pole, and Breit-Wigner peak. Validated across six orders of magnitude in energy, from $^5\text{He}$ to the Higgs boson, this rule predicts currently unknown residue phases: $-44(12)^\circ$ for $^5\mathrm{He}$, $-24(7)^\circ$ for $Σ(1385)^+$, and $-7(13)^\circ$ for $Ξ(1530)^0$. By inverting this formalism, we determine the $Υ(4S)$ pole from its empirical peak to be $10575(1)-i\,8.3(13)$ MeV, with a $-52(6)^\circ$ phase.
